accuracy.evidence: The levels cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism and the definitions used (a tissue is a group of similar cells with one job; an organ is several tissues working together; organs work together in a system) match the NC England KS3 biology statement on hierarchical organisation and BBC Bitesize 'Cells, tissues and organs'. Stomach tissues checked: smooth muscle churns food, the lining (epithelial and glandular tissue) makes gastric juice, and nerve tissue controls the muscle; it has no bone. System sorting checked: heart and blood vessels circulatory, stomach and intestines digestive, lungs and windpipe (trachea) breathing. The adult text notes that real tissues also hold some support cells, so 'similar cells' is not oversold.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented confusions about levels of organisation (Reiss and Tunnicliffe on children's ideas of internal body structure; the AAAS Project 2061 misconception that tissues are just any cells together, and the size confusion between tissue and organ): cells visible by eye (zoom predict, m1, tag 'see'), any mix of cells as a tissue (tissue predict, wrong-cell feedback, m6, tag 'mix'), one tissue per organ (organ predict, bone feedback, m2, tag 'organ'), tissue bigger than organ (ladder predict and order feedback, m3, tag 'size') and the heart in the breathing system (systems predict, sort feedback, m9, tag 'sys').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtissue models the nesting of body levels itself: a five-level zoom from the body through the circulatory system, the heart and heart muscle to one striped muscle cell with a breadcrumb trail; a tissue box that only accepts the cell kind it is building from a mixed tray of muscle, nerve and lining cells; a stomach that thickens a muscle wall, fills with lining and gains nerve lines as each tissue goes in; three system bins with their jobs; and a staircase that grows from cell to body. It is not a relabelled sorter.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds each rule by doing it: the box refuses a nerve cell while building muscle tissue, the stomach refuses bone, the heart will not go into the breathing system, and the staircase will not take 'organ' before 'tissue'. Each refusal says why, and the done message confirms the level rule only after the build is finished.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: seeing a cell 'if you look closely' (the zoom needs four steps and ends with 'too small to see by eye'), a tissue as 'all sorts of cells mixed up' (mixed cells are refused), an organ as 'just one' tissue (the stomach needs three), the heart in 'the breathing system, with the lungs' (it only sorts into circulatory) and 'a tissue' bigger than an organ (the staircase puts tissue on the lower step).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions whose wrong options map to six distinct messages: mix (similar cells, not any cells), one (a tissue is many cells), size (an organ is several tissues, so it is bigger), organ (tissues make an organ, organs make a system), sys (the lungs and windpipe make the breathing system) and see (cells need a microscope). The answer order rotates each question.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and builds the five curriculum terms one at a time with an example each (muscle tissue squeezes, the stomach is an organ, the heart and blood vessels are a system). FK grade is 4.5 for kid and 7.3 for adult, inside the family limits of 5.0 and 10.0. Canvas prompts give one action, such as 'Drag (or tap) the right cells into the box'.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: cells need a microscope, similar cells make a tissue, tissues make an organ (with the stomach's three), organs make systems. Adult paragraphs: curriculum placement and key words, a Lego model of the levels, five named mistakes plus the 'similar cells' caveat, and what each scene does. No stock phrases; the content gate's filler and 12% duplicate checks pass against the plant and animal cells lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark: the zoom ring is 40 to 100 px across and the five breadcrumbs fit one row; the 12 cell tiles sit in a 4 by 3 grid about 76 px wide with a full-width tissue box above; the four tissue cards are half-width with a one-line job under each name; the three system bins wrap their jobs to two lines and list sorted organs below; the staircase labels wrap 'Organ system' onto two lines. The iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Zoom in on the heart / heart wall / muscle cell', 'Add a muscle cell / nerve cell / lining cell', 'Add muscle tissue' (and lining, bone, nerve), 'Put the heart in the circulatory system' for each organ and system, and one button per level card. The canvas aria-label reports each result; axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
